chapter_title: Concerning the worn and torn apart Garments, or th

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
You must take in the inner meaning of these things. What is called the supreme investing is the sufficient fullness of ordered faculties of understanding that complete the integrated spiritual form of manifested glory, the fully formed heavenly human; and these faculties were cleansed and put into right order by the descent of a Divine mediation that brought purification into reception.

But what is called the torn investing is the enlightening power of understanding after it has been seized and consumed. It has been mixed and knotted into the outermost structure of the whole domain of lower life within dominating falsities and evils that rule in the higher external regions and extend through every successive level of outward consciousness. Its remaining brilliance is the scattered illumination that still flashes within the most external knowledges and within the regular operations of those outward forces. In the same way this seized illumination is also knotted into the lowest degrees, within the ultimate boundary where all things are held in check and weighed, and within the lowest natural level subject to that final restraint. It is called torn because it has been broken from its proper order and fixed in a damaged outward state.

What is called the greatly worn and torn investing is this same living illumination in bondage: it is gathered forcibly, divided, and consumed, and it is brought under the dominance of a sufficient series of merely bodily and sensual states that insinuate themselves and shift through outward forms, taking possession as they go.

And what is called the images and the great tattered investings are the full set of universal coverings of life in the lower degrees: the forms of love, the forms of truth, and the forms of their operation in outward life. The Living Divine invested these upon its manifested working, and by them arranged and stabilized everything in the whole domain of lower existence. By them also it cleared out the containing forms in the external region, purged them, and exposed their interiors at the ultimate threshold that stands at the base and support of all lower things.

What is called the fundamental principles is the same power of life that still remains in everything beneath. It rises up from the inmost receptacles of the lowest degrees, drawing itself together and then flowing out by influx into all things.

And what is called the Cross of Light is bound illumination held in restraint and extension, spread through the whole lowest domain, within states deprived of truth and within states that still receive truth.

And what is called the counsel of life is directing influx together with responsive reception. It moves within all these powers that have been named: it rouses them, grants them relief from pressure, and impels them into their proper activity.

What is called the soul that is slain—pressed down and destroyed—is the living power that should bring forth uses from inward truth: the capacity to produce works from perceptions, to generate beginnings of good and truth, and to sustain growth from them. These capacities are forcibly broken, uprooted, and cut off, and thus they become nourishment for merely bodily and sensual states. And when inward vitality is absent and outward truth has been ruined, what should have served life is lost; this too belongs to the same destroyed life, because even that whole portion is subjected to destruction.

For all these names are one in origin and one in their beginning: a single enlightening power as it shines forth. Yet in the first spiritual conflict it was divided into many parts, fixed into altered states, and so manifested as many appearances and many designations. But if these variations are uncovered and the outward show is removed, and the divided designations are put away, they will be gathered back into unity, forming one undivided state and one unchangeable identity forever within the plane of their first being, from which they first went forth to stand against what opposes the Divine.

paragraph_translations.notes: "Five worlds of the flesh" is rendered as a sufficient series of bodily-sensual states; the exact taxonomy of five is kept by meaning rather than listing.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by describing illumination stretched through the whole external plane under constraint.
paragraph_translations.notes: "Dry and moist" required an abstract rendering as deprivation/reception of truth; the 'cross' is kept as intersecting extension rather than any material sign.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strong coherence: the chapter consistently treats one enlightening power under different outward conditions—purified wholeness, capture and dispersion, Divine ordering through universal forms, remaining immanent vitality, restrained extension through the lowest plane, and coordinating influx—then returns all multiplicity to original unity. Minor strain arises where the source’s cosmological geography and corrupted terms force functional paraphrase, but the spiritual narrative remains continuous and single-voiced.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential definition: the chapter opens by defining a ‘garment’ as a functional complex that ‘makes perfect’ a body, and purification is explained by what the Ambassador’s coming does (purifies). No jurisdictional list or governance overlay intrudes.
findings.evidence: Text: “the five intellectuals that make perfect the body of the Pillar of Glory… They were purified by the coming of the Ambassador.” The spiritual reading had no stumble here and could narrate it directly as “ordered faculties… cleansed… by the descent of a Divine mediation.” That ease indicates the spiritual sense arises from function (making perfect/purifying), not administration.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential, with a localized textual difficulty (cosmological topography + probable lacuna) that forces paraphrase. The narrative does not break, but the geography (“rulers… firmaments… stars… chain… course… three earths… above the head of the Porter… under the Porter”) is descriptive rather than functional and is hard to integrate without re-mapping terms. This is not an insertion; it reads like the substrate’s cosmology plus damaged wording at the end.
findings.evidence: Text piles placements: “in the rulers who are above, who exist in all the firmaments… displayed in the stars of the chain and the powers of the course… entangled in these three earths below, above the head of the Porter… on the earth that is under the Porter.” Then a broken causal clause: “because [it has been torn away…] set [and has been fastened…]”. The reading explicitly notes strain: “some specific placements (‘above the head of the Porter’) resist exactness but yield a coherent sense…”. That is exactly what a damaged/topographical stretch produces: the reader must generalize to keep the story moving.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential continuation. Even the number ‘five’ functions descriptively (the flesh-worlds overpower) rather than as a ranked inventory. No named administrators appear; the ‘worlds’ are acting forces (“creep… move from place to place”).
findings.evidence: Text: “It is reaped, cut, and devoured… overpowered by the five worlds of the flesh, which creep as they move from place to place.” The reading reports no narrative rupture and could treat it as process (“further exhausted… roaming sensual dominion”), which is characteristic of substrate teaching by states and actions.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential triad with mild interpretive strain caused by element-names, not by a foreign administrative voice. The passage explains what the garments DO: they are ‘cloaked’, used to ‘set in order’, used to ‘empty the vessels’, ‘swept out’, ‘laid bare’—all functional operations tied to cosmic cleansing.
findings.evidence: Text: “the three great garments of the wind, the fire, and the water… With them he set in order things… emptied the vessels… swept them out and laid them bare.” The reading notes it had to translate the triad functionally (“wind, fire, water” rendered as love/truth/operation) to avoid over-literal naturalism: that is an exegetical choice under a stable functional narrative, not a sign of interpolation.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from corruption at the key term, but still correspondential in movement-description. The odd bracketed form (“‘[the elements]ments’”) indicates a damaged or miscopied lexeme; however the sentence that follows is coherent and functional (remaining power rises, gathers, pours forth).
findings.evidence: Text: “Conversely, ‘[the elements]ments’… are this power that remains… It rises up… gathering together, and pouring forth…” The reading explicitly flags corruption: “The source term is corrupt (‘[the elements]ments’); translated by function…” This is classic scribal damage/uncertain restoration rather than an administrative overlay.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential statement with an idiom that requires functional re-expression. The ‘Cross’ is defined by what it does (stretched/spread through all things), and “dry and moist” is a natural pair that can be abstracted without narrative break.
findings.evidence: Text: “the ‘[Light] Cross’… this bound ‘light power’. It [is stretched out]… upon the earth, in the dry and the moist.” The reading notes only an idiomatic strain: “‘Dry and moist’ required an abstract rendering… the ‘cross’ is kept as intersecting extension.” No intrusion of rank, jurisdiction, or named governors.

findings.diagnosis: Administrative-style institutional mechanism inserted into an otherwise correspondential sequence of functional definitions. ‘Counsel of life’ is redefined as a bureaucratic dyad (“summons and obedience”), a Mani-typical seam term. It does not arise from natural function, but from an institutional governance model; it reads like a doctrinal gloss that recasts the preceding powers as things to be ‘summoned’ and made to ‘obey’.
findings.evidence: Text: “the ‘counsel of life’ is the summons and the obedience. It moves in all these powers… awakens them… drives them to their movement.” The spiritual reading smooths it into correspondential language (“directing influx together with responsive reception”), but this is a translation rescue: the underlying phrasing is governance/command. This matches the developer’s seam markers (“institutional mechanism (‘counsel of life,’ ‘summons-and-obedience’)”). The story of one light-power in various states (¶7–12, ¶14–15) would read continuously if this sentence were absent; ¶13 is the one place the chapter stops naming conditions of the light and instead introduces a control protocol.
findings.scope: “Also, the one named the ‘counsel of life’ is the summons and the obedience.”

findings.diagnosis: After removing the institutional gloss, the remaining verbs can be read as correspondential (animation/relief/impulsion) describing how the named powers are activated. This looks like the substrate line to which the administrative definition was prefixed.
findings.evidence: Text after the gloss: “It moves in all these powers that we have named. It awakens them, gives them ease, and drives them to their movement.” These are functional effects consistent with the chapter’s process-language. The reader’s narrative treated ¶13 as continuous (“animating governance that coordinates…”), which becomes straightforward if the ‘summons/obedience’ bureaucratic identification is removed.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty due to image-collision and probable dittography/lacunae, not an administrative insertion. The paragraph abruptly stacks agricultural (‘fruit, vegetables and seeds’), craft/material (‘wood… dry’), and textile (‘garment… ragged’) images, then repeats killing language with broken syntax. This reads like conflation of exempla or a damaged copying of parallel clauses.
findings.evidence: Text: “power of fruit, vegetables and seeds… Further: the wood should it be dry, and the garment should it become ragged, will perish. Again, it is [a part]rt… since also even this whole part of it they kill [as they also kill it]”. The reading admits the strain and has to unify metaphorically: “The source mixes several images… unified here…”. That is the hallmark of a difficult/compounded transmission, but removing any one image does not clearly restore a cleaner administrative/correspondential boundary; the whole paragraph is still about what the ‘slain soul’ becomes/do (nourishes the flesh-worlds).

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential resolution and reintegration: multiplicity of names is explained as one power divided in contest and then regathered by stripping appearances. The closing battle-language is not administrative jurisdiction; it serves the functional narrative of dispersion and return.
findings.evidence: Text: “all these names… are a single power… they separated into all these parts in this first contest… if… laid bare… they will gather together and make a single form.” The reading reports coherence and closure (“resolving multiplicity back into original unity”), indicating no narrative stumble here.

textual_criticism.summary: 10 findings: the chapter is overwhelmingly correspondential and narratively continuous. Two genuine textual-difficulty zones appear (¶11 corrupt key term; ¶14 conflated/fragmentary imagery). One clear administrative seam/gloss occurs in ¶13 (“counsel of life” = “summons and obedience”), matching Mani-typical institutional mechanism; recommended excision of that exact definitional sentence, while retaining the following functional animation verbs. No other excisions recommended; no large overlay blocks detected.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: “It is proper for you to understand this. The garments that are named ‘great garment’ are the five intellectuals that make perfect the body of the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. They were purified by the coming of the Ambassador.

“In contrast, the ones named ‘rag’: the rags are the devoured enlightening power. It is compounded and entangled in the body of the universe in the rulers who are above, who exist in all the firmaments. Also, its shine is that which lights up and is displayed in the stars of the chain and the powers of the course. And likewise, these rags that are entangled in these three earths below, above the head of the Porter [at the foundation of all things] on the earth that is under the Porter. These are named the ‘rags’, because [it has been torn away from its own order,] set [and has been fastened in an outward damaged form]

“However, the ‘great worn and torn apart garments’, which we have proclaimed, is this entangled living power. It is reaped, cut, and devoured. It is overpowered by the five worlds of the flesh, which creep as they move from place to place.

“On the other hand, [these] we have termed the ‘images and the great tattered clothes’ [which we have proclaimed,] are the three great garments of the wind, the fire, and the water. These the Living Spirit cloaked upon his body. With them he set in order things in the universe. With them also he emptied the vessels. He swept them out and laid them bare in front of the Porter at the foundation of all things.

“Conversely, ‘[the elements]ments’, we have called them this name, are this power that remains in all things below. It rises up in the wombs of all the earths, gathering together, and pouring forth upon all things.
“And then, the ‘[Light] Cross’ [we have termed] this bound ‘light power’. It [is stretched out] all [things] upon the earth, in the dry and the moist.
“Also, it moves in all these powers that we have named. It awakens them, gives them ease, and drives them to their movement.

“The one named ‘the soul that is slain’, which is killed, oppressed and murdered; it is this power of fruit, vegetables and seeds. They shall be threshed, plucked and cut down; and they give nourishment to the worlds of the flesh. Further: the wood should it be dry, and the garment should it become ragged, will perish. Again, it is [a part]rt of this entire soul that is slain and killed; since also even this whole part of it they kill [as they also kill it]

“For all these names [that we have proclaimed] are a single [power,] since the beginning, it [was one power of light] as it enlightens; but they separated into all these parts in this first contest. They became set in all these altered forms, and these many names. Of course, if now all these varieties are laid bare, and stripped of all these appearances, and parted from all these names; they will gather together and make a single form, and a single name, unaltered and unchangeable for ever in the land of their first essence, from which they were sent forth against the enemy.”

changes_summary: Implemented Finding 7 (¶13) excision by removing the administrative definitional clause “Also, the one named the ‘counsel of life’ is the summons and the obedience.” Per Finding 8, retained the remaining functional animation statements (“It moves… awakens… gives… drives…”). No other paragraphs were modified (all other findings recommended none).
